change_description: Return to the iteration-1 terminal 0.30 execution-price-floor candidate and keep its exact five selected trades, but evaluate those trades at a fixed candidate position size of 1.0 instead of 0.2. Preserve the frozen v6.7 baseline at its original 0.2 size. Do not change the controller, threshold, feature inputs, selected action identities, cost model, or position lifecycle.
expected_mechanism: The iteration-1 selected set contained five positive after-cost trades and passed the absolute, largest-winner-removal, temporal-half, support, and safety gates. Applying the existing 1.0 runtime size to only those already-selected trades should scale their positive contribution while leaving every rejected market at zero, potentially moving the paired bootstrap LCB above zero without broadening support into the negative-edge recovery population exposed by iteration 2. This is historical development only and can never be promotion evidence.
mechanistic_rationale: Iteration 1 failed only the paired 97.5% LCB, which was -0.15145125 despite a +1.33240 point delta; its five retained trades had +0.23675 total after-cost PnL and remained +0.15680 after removing the largest winner. Iteration 2 showed that increasing support by recovering 129 high-price v6.7 actions destroyed absolute edge. The next bounded hypothesis therefore keeps the proven sparse selection fixed and changes only exposure. A fixed 1.0 size is preregistered because it is the existing paper-runtime default maximum, not a value selected from an exact-195 result grid.
